items.title: Finite extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: A finite extension is a field extension whose degree is finite.

items.title: Degree of an extension (field theory)
items.excerpt: Given an extension E/F, the field E can be considered as a vector space over the field F, and the dimension of this vector space is the degree of the extension, denoted by [E: F].

items.title: Extension field (field theory)
items.excerpt: If F is a subfield of E then E is an extension field of F. We then also say that E/F is a field extension.

items.title: Prime field (field theory)
items.excerpt: The prime field of the field F is the unique smallest subfield of F.

items.title: Subfield (field theory)
items.excerpt: A subfield of a field F is a subset of F which is closed under the field operation + and of F and which, with these operations, forms itself a field.

items.title: Characteristic (field theory)
items.excerpt: The characteristic of the field F is the smallest positive integer n such that n·1 = 0; here n·1 stands for n summands 1 + 1 + 1 +... + 1. If no such n exists, we say the character…

items.title: Zero divisor (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A zero divisor in a ring is an element whose product with some nonzero element is 0.

items.title: Weierstrass ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Weierstrass ring is local ring that is Henselian, pseudo-geometric, and such that any quotient ring by a prime ideal is a finite extension of a regular local ring.

items.title: Weak (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. Weak dimension is an alternative name for flat dimension of a module.

items.title: Valuation (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A valuation is a homomorphism from the non-zero elements of a field to a totally ordered abelian group, with properties similar to the p-adic valuation of the rational numbers.

items.title: Unramified morphism (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An unramified morphism of rings is a homomorphism that is formally unramified and finitely presented. These are analogous to immersions in differential topology. An algebra over…

items.title: Unmixed (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An ideal I of a ring R is called unmixed if all associated primes of R/I have the same height.

items.title: Universal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A universal field is an algebraically closed field with the uncountable transcendence degree over its prime field.

items.title: Universally catenary (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A property is said to hold universally if it holds for various base changes. For example a ring is universally catenary if all finitely generated algebras over it are catenary.

items.title: Unique factorization domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Also called a factorial domain. A unique factorization domain is an integral domain such that every element can be written as a product of primes in a way that is unique up to orde…

items.title: Unimodular row (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A sequence of elements $v_{1},\dots,v_{n}$ in a ring that generate the unit ideal.

items.title: Unibranch (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A reduced local ring is called unibranch if it is integral and its integral closure is a local ring. A local ring is called unibranch if the corresponding reduced local ring is uni…

items.title: Type (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The type of a finitely generated module M of depth d over a Noetherian local ring R with residue field k is the dimension (over k) of Extd R(k,M).

items.title: Trivial (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A trivial ring is a ring with only one element.

items.title: Total ring of fractions (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The total ring of fractions or total quotient ring of a ring is formed by forcing all non zero divisors to have inverses.

items.title: Torsion element (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A torsion element of a module over a ring is an element annihilated by some regular element of the ring.

items.title: Tor (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Torsion functors, the derived functors of the tensor product.

items.title: Tight closure (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The tight closure I of an ideal I of a ring with positive characteristic p0 consists of the elements z such that there is some c not in any minimal prime ideal such that czq is in…

items.title: Tangent (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Zariski tangent space of a local ring is the dual of its cotangent space.

items.title: Syzygy (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An element of the kernel of one of the maps in a free resolution of a module.

items.title: System of parameters (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A set of dim R (if finite) elements of a local ring R with maximal ideal m that generates an m-primary ideal. It is a regular system of parameters if it actually generates m.

items.title: Symbolic power (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The symbolic power p(n) of a prime ideal p is the set of elements x such that xy is in pn for some y not in p. It is the smallest p-primary ideal containing pn.

items.title: Support of a module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The support of a module M is the set of prime ideals p such that the localization of M at p is non-zero.

items.title: Superheight (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The superheight of an ideal is the supremum of the nonzero codimensions of the proper extensions of the ideal under ring homomorphisms.

items.title: Superfluous (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A submodule M of N is called superfluous if M+X=N implies X=N (for submodules X).

items.title: Strictly local (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A ring is called strictly local if it is a local Henselian ring whose residue field is separably closed.

items.title: Stably free (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A module M over a ring R is called stably free if M⊕Rn is free for some natural number n.

items.title: Stable (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A decreasing filtration of a module is called stable (with respect to an ideal I) if Mn+1=IMn for all sufficiently large n.

items.title: Socle of a module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The socle of a module is the sum of its simple submodules.

items.title: Smooth morphism (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A smooth morphism of rings is a homomorphism that is formally smooth and finitely presented. These are analogous to submersions in differential topology. An algebra over a ring is…

items.title: Simple field (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A simple field is an archaic term for an algebraic number field whose ring of integers is a unique factorization domain.

items.title: Separated (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An alternative term for Hausdorff, usually applied to a topology on a ring or module.

items.title: Separable (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An algebra over a field is called separable if its extension by any finite purely inseparable extension is reduced.

items.title: Seminormal ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A seminormal ring is a commutative reduced ring in which, whenever x, y satisfy $x^{3}=y^{2}$, there is s with $s^{2}=x$ and $s^{3}=y$.

items.title: Semi-local (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A semilocal ring is a ring with only a finite number of maximal ideals.

items.title: Saturation (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The saturation of a subset of a ring or module is the smallest saturated subset containing it.

items.title: Saturated (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A subset X of a ring or module is called saturated with respect to a multiplicative subset S if xs in X and s in S implies that x is in X.

items.title: Sn (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The condition Sn on a ring (for a non-negative integer n) says that the depth of the localization at any prime ideal is the height of the prime ideal whenever the depth is less tha…

items.title: Resolution of a module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A resolution of a module is a chain complex whose only non-zero homology group is the module.

items.title: Residue field (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The quotient of a ring, especially a local ring, by a maximal ideal.

items.title: Regularity (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity is an invariant of a graded module over a graded ring related to the vanishing of various cohomology groups.

items.title: Regular local ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A regular local ring is a Noetherian local ring whose dimension is equal to the dimension of its tangent space.

items.title: Reflexive (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A module M is reflexive if the canonical map $M\to M^{**},m\mapsto \langle \cdot,m\rangle$ is an isomorphism.

items.title: Reduced ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A reduced ring is one with no non-zero nilpotent elements.

items.title: Rank (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. Another older name for the height of a prime ideal.

items.title: Ramification group (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A ramification group is a group of automorphisms of a ring R fixing some given prime ideal p and acting trivially on R/pn for some integer n1. (When n=1 it is called the inertia gr…

items.title: Rn (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The condition Rn on a ring (for a non-negative integer n), "regular in codimension n", says that localization at any prime ideal of height at most n is regular. (cf. Serre's criter…

items.title: Quotient (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A quotient of a ring by an ideal, or of a module by a submodule.

items.title: Quasi (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A quasi-excellent ring is a Grothendieck ring such that for every finitely generated algebra the singular points of the spectrum form a closed subset.

items.title: Purely inseparable (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. An element x is purely inseparable over a field if either the field has characteristic zero and x is in the field or the field has characteristic p and $x^{p^{r}}$ is in the fie…

items.title: Pure submodule (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A pure submodule M of a module N is a submodule such that M⊗A is a submodule of N⊗A for all modules A.

items.title: Pseudo (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A finitely generated module M is called pseudo-zero if $M_{\mathfrak {p}}=0$ for all prime ideals ${\mathfrak {p}}$ of height $\leq 1$.

items.title: Prüfer domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Prüfer domain is a semiherediary integral domain.

items.title: Projective module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A projective module is a module such that every epimorphism to it splits.

items.title: Principal ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A principal ideal is an ideal generated by one element.

items.title: Primary ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A primary ideal is a proper ideal p of a ring R such that if rm is in p then either m is in p or some power of r is in p. More generally a primary submodule of a module M is a s…

items.title: Prime ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A prime ideal is a proper ideal whose complement is closed under multiplication.

items.title: Presentable (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A presentable ring is one that is a quotient of a regular ring.

items.title: Place of a field (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A place of a field K with values in a field L is a map from K∪∞ to L∪∞ preserving addition and multiplication and 1.

items.title: Picard group (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Picard group Pic(R) of a ring R is the group of isomorphism classes of finite projective modules of rank 1.

items.title: Perfect ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: In non-commutative ring theory, perfect ring has an unrelated meaning.

items.title: Parafactorial (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Noetherian local ring R is called parafactorial if it has depth at least 2 and the Picard group Pic(Spec(R) − m) of its spectrum with the closed point m removed is trivial.

items.title: Orientation (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An orientation of a module over a ring R is an isomorphism from the highest non-zero exterior power of the module to R.

items.title: Normally flat (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A module M over a ring R is called normally flat along an ideal I if the R/I-module ⊕InM/In+1M is flat.

items.title: Normal domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A normal domain is an integral domain that is integrally closed in its quotient field.

items.title: Nilradical (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The nilradical of a ring is the ideal of nilpotent elements.

items.title: Nilpotent (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Some power is zero. Can be applied to elements of a ring or ideals of a ring. See nilpotent.

items.title: Nagata ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Nagata ring is a Noetherian universally Japanese ring. These are also called pseudo-geometric rings.

items.title: N-2 ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An N-2 ring is the same as a Japanese ring, in other words an integral domain whose integral closure in any finite extension of its quotient field is a finitely generated module.

items.title: N-1 ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An N-1 ring is an integral domain whose integral closure in its quotient field is a finitely generated module.

items.title: Multiplicity (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The multiplicity of a module M at a prime ideal p or a ring R is the number of times R/p occurs in M, or more precisely the length of the localization Mp as a module over Rp.

items.title: Multiplicative subset (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A subset of a ring closed under multiplication

items.title: Mori domain (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Mori domain is an integral domain satisfying the ascending chain conditions on integral divisorial ideals.

items.title: Monomial (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A product of powers of generators of an algebra

items.title: Mittag-Leffler condition (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Mittag-Leffler condition is a condition on an inverse system of modules that ensures the vanishing of the first derived functor of the inverse limit.

items.title: Miracle (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. Miracle flatness is another name for Hironaka's criterion, which says that a local ring that is finite over a regular local ring is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if it is a flat mo…

items.title: Minimal prime (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A minimal prime of an ideal is a minimal element of the set of prime ideals containing it.

items.title: Maximal ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A maximal ideal is a maximal element of the set of proper ideals of a ring.

items.title: Lying over property (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An extension of rings has the lying over property if the corresponding map between their prime spectra is surjective.

items.title: Locally (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. A local ring is a ring with just one maximal ideal. In older books it is sometimes also assumed to be Noetherian.

items.title: Linkage (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A relation between ideals in a Gorenstein ring.

items.title: Linearly disjoint (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: Two subfields of a field extension K over a field k are called linearly disjoint if the natural map from their tensor product over k to the subfield of K they generate is an isomor…

items.title: Length of a module (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The length of a module is the length of any composition series.

items.title: Laskerian ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Laskerian ring is a ring in which any ideal has a primary decomposition.

items.title: Krull ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Krull ring (or Krull domain) is a ring with a well behaved theory of prime factorization.

items.title: Koszul complex (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Koszul complex is a free resolution constructed from a regular sequence.

items.title: Kleinian integer (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The Kleinian integers are the integers of the imaginary quadratic field of discriminant −7.

items.title: Kähler differential (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The module of Kähler differentials of a ring is the universal module with a derivation from the ring to it.

items.title: Japanese ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A Japanese ring (also called N-2 ring) is an integral domain R such that for every finite extension L of its quotient field K, the integral closure of R in L is a finitely generate…

items.title: Jacobian matrix (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: 1. The Jacobian matrix is a matrix whose entries are the partial derivatives of some polynomials.

items.title: J-2 ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A J-2 ring is a ring such that any finitely generated algebra is a J-1 ring.

items.title: J-1 ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A J-1 ring is a ring such that the set of regular points of the spectrum is an open subset.

items.title: J-0 ring (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: A J-0 ring is a ring such that the set of regular points of the spectrum contains a non-empty open subset.

items.title: Isolated prime (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: An isolated prime of a module is a minimal associated prime.

items.title: Irrelevant ideal (commutative algebra)
items.excerpt: The irrelevant ideal of a graded algebra is generated by all elements of positive degree.
